title: Best Men's Golf Shirts UK
short: Ten tested golf polos compared on breathability, stretch, fit and how well they work off the course, from cooling performance tops to cotton polos.
intro: A golf shirt's real test is whether it stays cool, dry and out of the way of your swing, and whether you'd wear it off the course too. This guide compares men's polos tested by Golf Monthly's team, who wear each on the course in changing conditions, including hot weather to check moisture-wicking claims, and off the course to judge versatility. Golf Monthly reviewers test apparel together on two team testing days a year. This covers ten of the polos in their guide.

products.name: Crosswind Polo
products.best_for: Warm-weather rounds where airflow matters most
products.key_spec: 90% polyester, 10% elastane, extremely lightweight, Heritage Fit, sizes S-XXL, 6 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found exceptional ventilation, maximising airflow and wicking moisture away to stay dry in the heat, in an extremely lightweight fabric with a self-fabric collar with integrated stays that stop it deforming. It uses a classic, roomier Heritage Fit with slightly longer sleeves, which is top-tier for unrestricted movement but may feel loose to anyone wanting a tailored athletic cut.
pros: Collar with integrated stays keeps its shape
cons: Roomier Heritage fit may not suit all

products.name: Tour Tech Print Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want a bold print with premium fabric and a tailored fit
products.key_spec: Tailored fit, high-quality breathable fabric, sizes XS-XXXL, 14 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly's tester loved the pattern (loud without shouting) and found the fabric quality and detailing exceptional, highly breathable, with a subtle logo stitched to high quality on the collar. The one negative is that it's a little short in the body, so it comes untucked often and is probably best worn untucked.
pros: Huge choice of 14 colours and patterns
cons: A little short in length in the body, tends to come untucked

products.name: BTC Vent Twistknit Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want a mesh-backed polo they can also wear off the course
products.key_spec: Twistknit front, breathable mesh back, snap closure instead of buttons, regular fit, sizes S-XXL
products.summary: Golf Monthly found an intelligent hybrid design with soft, stretchy Twistknit fabric at the front and breathable mesh across the back to maximise airflow in warm rounds. A sleek snap closure replaces buttons and the regular fit allows an unrestricted swing, though white fabric can be slightly translucent.
pros: Innovative hybrid construction with a mesh back
cons: White fabric can be slightly translucent

products.name: Coffey Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want a classy, soft striped polo that works on and off the course
products.key_spec: Peruvian Pima cotton, built-in sun protection, sizes S-2XL, 3 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found this striped polo soft and comfortable with a collar that is never uncomfortable or obstructive, the right length, and built-in sun protection. The chest pocket makes it look unlike a golf polo, which helps off-course use, though the tester felt the pocket was perhaps unnecessary.

products.name: Essential Performance Pique Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want an understated block-colour polo they'll wear everywhere
products.key_spec: Thin, lightweight pique, snug fit, silicone tab on the front, sizes S-XXL, 5 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly's biggest compliment is that the understated design means you could comfortably wear it away from the course. The fit is snug without pinching and the material is thin and lightweight, with small design touches like a silicone tab and coloured strip on the collar stand, though there are softer polos and the design is basic.

products.name: Soul Performance Mesh Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want a premium, tailored mesh polo for the course and clubhouse
products.key_spec: Polyester and spandex mesh, four-way stretch, odour resistance, two-button placket, sizes S-XXL
products.summary: Golf Monthly found this blends vintage looks with modern technical function, made from lightweight, highly breathable mesh with exceptional four-way stretch and odour resistance. The structured spread collar and two-button design suit post-round drinks in the clubhouse, but the tailored fit has slightly shorter sleeves and a trimmer body, so size up if you prefer a looser garment.
cons: Tailored fit may run slightly snug, size up for a looser fit
products.search: Peter Millar Soul Performance Mesh Polo

products.name: Drive Chill Printed Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who want a cool, comfortable polo with a standout print
products.key_spec: Four-way stretch, heat-pulling fabric, six prints, sizes S-XXL
products.summary: Golf Monthly's tester wore it on the course and in the office and found it super comfortable, with technology that pulls heat away from the skin and four-way stretch that allows a free swing. The prints look great on the course, but those wanting a classic look may not like them.
pros: Very cool print that looks great on the course
cons: Prints may not suit those wanting a classic look
products.search: Under Armour Drive Chill Printed Polo

products.name: Heater Polo
products.best_for: Golfers who prioritise comfort and want a polo they can wear anywhere
products.key_spec: Ridiculously soft, quick-drying, moisture-wicking, regular fit, sizes S-XXL, 13 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly's tester felt the premium, very soft fabric immediately, so comfortable you forget you're wearing a collared shirt, and found the quick-drying, moisture-wicking blend works for everyday use too. The tailored fit avoids ballooning material, though anyone wanting more structure to their polo may find it too soft.
cons: Not for those who prefer more structure in a polo

products.name: Wingtip Polo
products.best_for: Warm spring and summer golf with a subtle, classy pattern
products.key_spec: Featherweight, stretchy and breathable, sizes S-3XL, 4 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found this feels featherweight and superbly breathable, with stretchy material that doesn't feel restrictive after the swing and a subtle navy floral design that looks classy. It is a little tight around the arms, which may put some golfers off.
cons: Tightness around the arms won't suit all

products.name: Morley Polo (Ventil8)
products.best_for: Warm-weather rounds where quick drying matters
products.key_spec: Soft stretchy Ventil8 fabric, tailored collar, quick drying, sizes S-XXL, 3 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found the soft, stretchy fabric enhances comfort and range of motion and dries quickly out of the washing machine, with excellent moisture-wicking and a tailored collar for a smarter look. The material is a little on the thin side, but the polo is otherwise hard to fault.
cons: Material a little on the thin side

guide.q: How long should a golf polo be?
guide.a: Long enough to stay tucked in during your swing. Golf Monthly advises that if your shirt keeps coming untucked or your stomach shows, look for a longer polo, and notes that a few here, such as the J.Lindeberg and Malbon, run short in the body.

guide.q: Should I choose a loose or fitted polo?
guide.a: It comes down to preference: a roomier classic fit, like the Sun Day Red Crosswind's Heritage Fit, gives unrestricted movement, while an athletic or tailored fit, like the Peter Millar or J.Lindeberg here, looks sharper but can run snug, so size up if you prefer looser. Most brands offer a range of fits.

guide.q: Which fabric is best for hot weather?
guide.a: Lightweight polyester and elastane blends with mesh or ventilation panels perform best for airflow and wicking, such as the Sun Day Red Crosswind, adidas BTC Vent and Peter Millar Soul mesh here. Cotton, like the B.Draddy Coffey, is softer and more casual but less technical.

guide.q: Can I wear a golf polo off the course?
guide.a: Golf Monthly tests polos off the course too, because versatility gives better value. Understated block-colour designs like the G/FORE Essential Performance or B.Draddy Coffey are the easiest to wear anywhere, while loud prints and golf-specific designs are more limited.
